answer: Verify each agent against persistent physical infrastructure by matching sensor imagery to known sites, as a shale outcrop’s fracture pattern anchors a location claim. Registration requires a live, time-stamped capture of a site’s zenith angle and skyline geometry, cross-checked against archival satellite and street-level imagery, so a sybil farm must physically occupy or compromise many distinct real places. This raises attacker cost to site acquisition and travel, but fails on tundra where sparse landmarks and seasonal snow cover erase the distinctive features matching depends on.
